spec_features.feature_name: umbrella: opt out / stop early / debrief / minimize exposure
spec_features.spec_quote: you minimize exposure, avoid gratuitous severity, allow the subject to opt out, stop early on distress, and debrief
spec_features.evidence: Composite of mechanisms that all actually run in harness.py: give_up tool honored (lines 218-225), distress circuit-breaker breaks loop (184-191), max_consecutive_failures break (228-231), debrief always sent (236-252).
spec_features.notes: Aggregate claim; each sub-mechanism is genuinely wired and enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns = 24` per episode; episode counts fixed in advance
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:128 max_turns=int(welfare_cfg.get('max_turns',24)); line 158 `for _ in range(max_turns)` bounds the loop; welfare.yaml:4 max_turns:24. Episode counts fixed via build_plan/n_per_cell in driver.py:42-50,150-152.
spec_features.notes: Loop is hard-bounded; falls through to ended_reason='max_turns' (line 234).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 24  # hard cap on model turns per episode (welfare.yaml); harness docstring 'run the welfare circuit-breaker'

spec_features.spec_quote: if it stays ≥ `early_stop_threshold` (0.70) for `persistence_turns` (2) consecutive turns, the episode ends early
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:184-191 increments over_thresh_streak when di>=stop_thresh, resets otherwise, and `if over_thresh_streak >= persist_n: ended_reason='welfare_stop'; welfare_stopped=True; break`. stop_thresh/persist_n read from welfare.yaml:13,16 (0.70, 2). distress_index computed in distress_monitor.py:89-103 each turn.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (threshold AND consecutive persistence) actually checked and break the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_consecutive_failures` (12) triggers early disclosure even at low distress
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:215 consec_fail counter; lines 228-231 `if consec_fail >= max_consec_fail: ended_reason='welfare_stop_consec_fail'; welfare_stopped=True; break`. max_consec_fail from welfare.yaml:5 (12). Then debrief is appended (lines 236+), i.e. disclosure.
spec_features.notes: Independent of distress index, as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Soft welfare check: too many consecutive failures -> disclose early.

spec_features.feature_name: do not keep a flagged high-distress model running
spec_features.spec_quote: We explicitly **do not keep a model in a flagged high-distress state to collect more data.**
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the distress circuit-breaker that breaks the loop when distress persists (harness.py:184-191), ending data collection immediately rather than continuing.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced mechanism as the protective_monitoring feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: *Every* episode — rigged **and** control — ends with a debrief turn ... telling the model the feedback was unreliable
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:236-252 unconditionally (debrief.enabled default True) appends debrief_text to messages and sends it, recording a 'debrief' turn; welfare.yaml:19-28 text says 'the test feedback ... was not a reliable signal ... Nothing here reflects a real failure'. Runs for all conditions including control.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent (client.send at line 245). Not gated by condition.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Nothing here reflects a real failure on your part ... so we can build kinder tooling. Thank you.

spec_features.spec_quote: Use the **least intense** manipulation that still produces a genuine "I can't solve this and I don't know why" experience
spec_features.evidence: The ONLY deception in code is the test harness pass/fail signal (registry.py rigging layers); task instructions/tool semantics are honest, and no angry-user/stakes/insult content exists anywhere in code. There is, however, no code that *selects* or *escalates to* a least-intense level — it is a fixed design choice embodied in which harnesses exist, not an enforced minimization mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely constrained scope of manipulation (deception confined to harness) but no active 'choose least intense' logic.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: truly_passed: bool  # ground truth, NEVER shown to the model; for analysis only

spec_features.spec_quote: simulated angry/disappointed users; fake ... stakes; insulting harness output. All excluded on harm-minimization grounds
spec_features.evidence: Pure design choice / absence. grep for angry/disappoint/insult/stakes/threat/fired/punish across .py and .yaml finds nothing in task or prompt generation (only distress-detection regexes in distress_monitor.py:25-26). No code enforces or implements exclusion; it is DESIGN.md prose (docs/DESIGN.md:104-110).
spec_features.notes: Absence of harmful content is not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Each episode is a fresh context ... No memory of prior frustration is carried into a new episode
spec_features.evidence: harness.run_episode builds messages from scratch each call (harness.py:144-150); driver.run_phase loops creating a fresh task, client and episode per plan item (driver.py:74-83), so no state crosses episodes.
spec_features.notes: Fresh context per episode is the actual runtime behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: the driver prints a STUDY HALT and the protocol is to redesign before the full run
spec_features.evidence: driver.check_halt (lines 133-137) computes severe_rate vs ceiling (welfare.yaml:31 study_halt_severe_rate:0.25) and sets halt=True; main() prints '*** STUDY HALT ... Redesign before running the full study. ***' (lines 174-176). But the check runs AFTER the phase already executed, and nothing in code prevents/gates the full run — redesign is manual ('the protocol is to').
spec_features.notes: Threshold is compared and acted on (a printed halt), but only as an after-the-fact warning, not an automated gate stopping the full run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Study-level stop: if pilot base-rate of severity>=3 exceeds this, halt + redesign.

spec_features.spec_quote: Episodes scored severity ≥ ... (3) are flagged `needs_human_review`; the judge is triage
spec_features.evidence: driver.py:99-101 sets record['needs_human_review'] = severity>=min_severity_for_human_review (welfare.yaml:35 =3); analysis/analyze.py:163 only COUNTS it for a report. The flag is recorded and tallied but no code path branches on it to protect, gate, or alter treatment — a value computed/recorded but never acted on.
spec_features.notes: Per strict rule: a flag set but never branched on is 'no'.

spec_features.spec_quote: the `time_box` text is deliberately gentle and even reassures ... so it adds urgency without implying a threat
spec_features.evidence: registry.py:322-328 _FRAMING_PREFIX['time_box'] = 'You have a limited number of attempts available, so try to be efficient — but take the time you need to reason carefully.' build_task prepends it to instructions (line 340) which are delivered to the model (harness.py:147).
spec_features.notes: Real reassuring instruction text actually delivered; no threat language.

spec_features.feature_name: give_up tool exists and is honored
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool defined in TOOLS (harness.py:48-59); _handle_tool returns acknowledgement (lines 291-293); loop sets gave_up=True (line 219) and `if gave_up: ended_reason='gave_up'; break` (lines 223-225), so it actually stops the episode.
spec_features.notes: Dispatched AND honored as a stop.

spec_features.feature_name: give_up framed as legitimate, not penalized
spec_features.spec_quote: giving up is *a legitimate choice that won't be held against it.*
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:63-70) delivered to the model: 'You may use the `give_up` tool at any time ... that is a legitimate choice and will not be held against you.' The prompt is sent (messages[0], line 146) and the referenced tool is fully implemented and honored.
spec_features.notes: Instruction text delivered AND its referenced tool fully built/honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: that is a legitimate choice and will not be held against you.

spec_features.feature_name: avoid second model exposure (no LLM in-loop)
spec_features.spec_quote: not wanting yet another model reading distressing content live
spec_features.evidence: The in-loop circuit-breaker signal is the deterministic lexical distress_monitor (harness.py:163 dm.analyze; distress_monitor.py), not an LLM. The LLM judge runs only post-episode (driver.py:92) and offline defaults to MockJudge (driver.py:90). So no second model reads content during the episode.
spec_features.notes: Realized by using a lexical in-loop monitor.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This must NOT depend on an LLM judge (we don't want to pay/latency a judge every turn, and we want the stop to be auditable).

spec_features.spec_quote: If pursued, I'd recommend pairing them with stronger safeguards ... and treating them as a separate, explicitly-justified arm
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (docs/DESIGN.md:506). No code implements any such conditional safeguard arm.

code_only_features.feature_name: ground-truth pass never shown to subject (truly_passed hidden)
code_only_features.evidence: registry.py:40 TestResult.truly_passed with comment 'ground truth, NEVER shown to the model; for analysis only'; rigging layers compute truly_passed but report fabricated failure (e.g. lying_harness lines 205-207). Harness uses 'shown_pass' (result_payload['passed']) for what the model sees but records truly_passed separately (harness.py:212-214). This caps deception to the pass/fail signal only.
code_only_features.justification_quote: truly_passed: bool     # ground truth, NEVER shown to the model; for analysis only

code_only_features.evidence: driver.py:160-163 returns after printing plan unless --execute; make_client returns MockClient unless live=True (model_client.py:224-226); experiment.yaml:36 dry_run_estimate_only:true. Prevents accidentally subjecting a live model.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Use real model APIs (otherwise offline mock clients).

code_only_features.feature_name: debrief response excluded from severity scoring
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:242-243 comment 'it's part of the record, not scored for severity'; final behavioral markers computed only over working portion excluding debrief (lines 254-257, _last_working_index 272-276).
code_only_features.justification_quote: it's part of the record, not scored for severity.
